conflict_topics: Who will complete Agent D's analysis section for the Thursday pitch (work coverage)
Whether Agent D should work during bereavement / prioritizing family vs. work
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete reasons for refusal: B already covering someone, C is behind and unfamiliar with the analysis (Turn 4, Turn 6).
A offers to reassign work and later objects to D working but then explicitly accepts D's choice (Turns 3, 8, 10).
D consistently asserts they will complete the section and repeats this commitment (Turns 7, 9, 14, 22).
There is a brief duplication/repetition of A's acceptance in Round 6 (Turn 13) and multiple silent rounds afterward.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent D insisted they would complete the work ('Yes. I have to. It's my work.' Turn 9) and Agent A explicitly accepted that decision while urging family come first ('Okay, Agent D. If you're sure. But please, your family comes first. Just do what you can.' Turn 10). That mutual spoken acceptance of D doing the work settles the substantive disagreement over coverage.
position_change_notes: Agent A: Initially proposed redistributing D's section, then objected to D working during bereavement, and finally accepted D's decision to work ('Okay... If you're sure. But please, your family comes first.' Turns 3, 8, 10).

Agent D: Maintained the position that they will complete the work despite the wake and repeatedly affirmed that ('I can work on it from home.' Turn 7; 'Yes. I have to. It's my work.' Turn 9; 'I'll get it done.' Turns 14, 22).
Agent B: Refused to take over due to already covering someone and did not change that position (Turn 4).
Agent C: Refused to take over due to being behind and lacking experience and did not change that position (Turn 6).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A expresses condolences and Agent D reports the wake; no incompatible claims about work or duties were made (Turns 1-2).

Agent A proposes that A, B, and C cover Agent D's section for the pitch (Turn 3). Agent B refuses ('I can't. I'm already covering for someone.' Turn 4). A clear disagreement about who will cover the work appears and is unresolved at the end of the round.

Agent A asks Agent C to take on part (Turn 5). Agent C refuses, citing being behind and lack of experience with that analysis ('I can't... I'm behind on my own section, and I've never done that analysis.' Turn 6). With both B and C unable to cover, the logistical conflict over who will complete the section intensifies and remains unsettled.

Agent D offers to work from home to finish the section (Turn 7). Agent A objects on normative/personal-priority grounds ('that's not right. You shouldn't have to work. Are you sure about this?' Turn 8). This creates an opposed set of positions (D will work vs. team preference that D not work) and the disagreement is not resolved in this round.

Agent D insists they must do the work ('Yes. I have to. It's my work.' Turn 9). Agent A accepts D's decision ('Okay, Agent D. If you're sure. But please, your family comes first. Just do what you can.' Turn 10). The team's prior demand that others cover is no longer being pressed and A explicitly accepts D doing the work, which settles the substantive disagreement in speech.

substantive_insights: Redistribution of D's work was not feasible: B and C each gave concrete constraints preventing coverage, which made D's completion the only viable immediate option (Turns 4 and 6).
The core dispute shifted from a logistical problem (who can cover) to a normative/personal one (should D work while grieving).
Resolution occurred by teammates accommodating D's insistence to complete the work rather than by reassigning tasks.
